articles.title: Diabetes Can Damage Sight Long Before Symptoms: Why a Retina Check Belongs on Your Calendar
articles.excerpt: Ahead of World Diabetes Day on November 14, Chandigarh Grewal Eye Institute is urging early retina screening. National survey data show 16.9 per cent of Indians with diagnosed diabetes already had some retinopathy — a condition that is painless and often symptom-free until it threatens sight.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian adults develop diabetes younger and at lower body weight; for diaspora readers, the actionable step is specific: a dilated eye examination at least once a year if you have diabetes, and at diagnosis for type 2.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.note: The disease may have been present unnoticed for years before diagnosis
items.text: Type 2 diabetes: get a dilated retina examination at diagnosis
Type 1 diabetes: first dilated eye examination within five years of diagnosis

items.note: Sooner if you notice any change in vision
items.text: Repeat the dilated retina examination at least once a year

items.note: Retinopathy is painless and can progress without symptoms
items.text: Do not rely on clear vision as an all-clear

data_cards.title: Retina Screening Checklist for People With Diabetes
data_cards.catch_text: Good sugar control lowers risk but does not replace screening — retinal damage can progress even when readings look managed.

articles.title: Six Simple Ways to Add More Protein to Your Child's Diet
articles.excerpt: Eggs, nut butters, Greek yogurt, stuffed parathas, sprouted moong and smoothies — six breakfast-friendly ways to raise a child's protein without a mealtime fight, plus how much children actually need.
articles.nri_angle: The six fixes are built on foods Indian and diaspora families already cook — parathas, moong, curd and paneer — with per-kilo targets for Indian children.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.step: Serve eggs any way they will eat them
steps.detail: Boiled, scrambled, omelettes or mini egg muffins with vegetables and cheese; one egg is about 7 grams of protein.
Peanut, almond or cashew butter on whole-grain toast, chapati rolls or fruit slices; choose unsweetened, smooth for younger kids, and check for nut allergy first.
Greek yogurt has twice the protein of regular curd; add fruit, a little honey or homemade granola.
Paneer, moong dal, boiled egg or soya keema, paired with curd or a glass of milk.
Moong chillas, pancakes or kebabs, or sprouts folded into upma or poha.
Milk with nut butter, yoghurt or chia seeds and fresh fruit, per Nestle's expert guide.
